ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
A square single-turn coil is made of uniform wire with a side length of $0.3\mathrm{m}$. Two-thirds of the coil (i.e., the part to the left of the line $ab$) is in a uniform magnetic field directed perpendicularly into the plane of the paper, where $B=3T$.

1. When the magnetic field weakens at a rate of $10\mathrm{T/s}$, what is the magnitude of the induced electromotive force?
2. What is the induced electromotive force when the coil is about to leave the magnetic field with a horizontal velocity of $0.5\mathrm{m/s}$ to the right?

Two-thirds of the coil (i.e., the part to the left of the line $ab$) is in a uniform magnetic field directed perpendicularly into the plane of the paper, where $B=3T$. 1. When the magnetic field weakens at a rate of $10\mathrm{T/s}$, what is the magnitude of the induced electromotive force? 2. ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description first: The figure shows a square coil. A vertical dashed line labeled a at the top and b at the bottom divides the square, and the region to the left of this line contains several × symbols, indicating a uniform magnetic field into the page. Visually, this left region is two-thirds of the coil’s area, while the right third is outside the magnetic field. Reasoning: The square coil has side length L = 0.3 m, so its total area is L^2 = 0.09 m^2. Since only two-thirds of the coil is threaded by the magnetic field, the effective area is A = (2/3)L^2 = (2/3)(0.09) = 0.06 m^2. 1. For a fixed coil with changing magnetic field, Faraday’s law gives the magnitude of the induced emf as |ε| = A |dB/dt|. With |dB/dt| = 10 T/s, |ε| = 0.06 × 10 = 0.6 V. 2. When the coil moves rightward out of a constant magnetic field, the overlap area decreases at rate dA/dt = L v. Thus the magnitude of the induced emf is |ε| = B L v = 3 × 0.3 × 0.5 = 0.45 V.
